questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Romania?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Romania article.

questions.proof: The capital and biggest city in Romania is Bucharest (Romanian: București ), with a population of 1.6 million.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Romania?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Romania on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Romania article.

questions.proof: Most of Romania's border with Serbia and Bulgaria is made by the Danube.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Romania?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Language and culture” part of the Romania article.

questions.proof: The official language of Romania is Romanian.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Romania?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Social welfare” part of the Romania article.

questions.proof: By the first quarter of 2011 the average monthly household income is 2,318 Romanian leu (equivalent to approximately £862 USD).

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “At the end of World War II, some of its land (close by what is now known as _____) was occupied by the USSR.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “known”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Romania article.

questions.proof: At the end of World War II, some of its land (close by what is now known as Moldova) was occupied by the USSR.
